data.title: the Interaction Proteome of Ribosomal 40S Components PNO1 and NOB1 Using TurboID Proximity Labeling Technology
data.projectDescription: Background: The ribosome assembly factors PNO1 and NOB1 play crucial roles in the maturation of the 40S ribosomal small subunit. TurboID is an efficient biotin ligase that can biotinylate proteins in proximity to the target protein and is widely used to study complex biological processes within cells.Here, we utilized this technology to investigate the complex interaction network of PNO1 and NOB1 within cells.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: In order to prepare proteomic samples for mass spectrometry analysis, the proteins bound to chain affinity beads were washed with 200 μ L of 50 mM Tris hcl (pH 7.5), and then washed twice with 200 μ L of 2M urea in 50 mM Tris (pH 7.5) buffer. Add 80 μ L of 2 M urea to 50 mM Tris hcl containing 1 mM DTT and 0.4 μ g trypsin, incubate at 25 ° C for 1 hour, and shake at 1000 rpm. After 1 hour, remove the supernatant and transfer it to a new test tube. Wash the streptavidin beads twice in 50 mM Tris (pH 7.5) buffer with 60 μ L of 2m urea, and bind the washed streptavidin magnetic beads to the supernatant of the cell lysate. Add DTT to a final concentration of 4mm, reduce disulfide bonds in the eluent, and incubate at 25 ° C for 30 minutes, shaking at 1000 rpm. Add iodoacetamide to alkylate the eluent to a final concentration of 10mm, incubate in darkness at 25 ° C for 45 minutes, and shake at 1000 rpm. Add 0.5 μ g of trypsin to the sample, digest overnight at 25 ° C, and shake at 700 rpm. After overnight digestion, the sample was acidified by adding FA to make it contain~1% (vol/vol) FA, with a pH value of 3. Desalinate the sample using C18 StageTips. Centrifuge under vacuum at 4 ℃ until completely dry. Evaporate the sample in a vacuum concentrator until dry. Each sample was reconstructed in 9 μ L 0.1% (vol/vol) FA/3% (vol/vol) acetonitrile and placed in an HPLC-LC/MC automatic sampler.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: We use the Spectrum Mill MS Proteomics Workbench. Typical parameters used for searching data with Spectrum Mill are provided in the ‘Equipment setup’ section.  For the ratiometric approach, analyze each replicate separately and overlap the lists at the end to obtain a final proteome list. Begin with all proteins that were identified by two or more unique peptides.Generate lists of TP and FP proteins. For a three-state ratiometric analysis approach, two lists of FP proteins are required for two filtering steps: one for proteins that should not be biotinylated by TurboID and another for proteins that do not localize to the cellular compartment being analyzed.Comprehensive lists of TP and FP proteins can be generated by combining information from the Gene Ontology Cellular Component (GOCC) database, the UniProt database, and the literature.For example, for the analysis of proteomic data generated from ERM–TurboID, the first filter step compared ERM–TurboID with untransfected controls and used a FP list containing mitochondrial matrix proteins, whereas the second step compared ERM–TurboID with cytosolic TurboID–NES and used a FP list containing non-secretory system proteins. Normalize corresponding TMT ratios against the distribution of FP proteins that should not be biotinylated by TurboID. To do this, divide all TMT ratios by the median of the ratios for FP proteins. Calculate the log2 value of each ratio; log2 values will be used for the rest of the analysis.This normalization centers the distribution of the log2 ratios of nonspecifically binding proteins around 0. Check the correlation between replicates by plotting the corresponding log2 ratios.Rank the proteins by the appropriate TMT ratio values in descending order and cross this list with the TP and FP lists to determine which proteins are TPs and FPs, respectively. At each potential cutoff, calculate the TPR and FP rate (FPR), where the TPR/FPR is defined as the number of detected TP/FP proteins detected above the cutoff divided by the total number of detected TP/FP proteins in that replicate. A plot of the TPR versus the FPR should show that the curve bows out as compared with the diagonal, which shows that the proteomic experiment successfully enriched TP proteins over FP proteins. Determine the cutoff by using the log2 ratio that corresponds to the maximum TPR-FPR value. In cases in which the list of TP proteins is small , where FDR is defined as the fraction of FP proteins detected above each cutoff. Retain all proteins with log2 ratios higher than that of the determined cutoff.
